note: Headless, run by Claude on the bench harness (M3 Pro, DPR=2, vsync-capped lane, vite 5173 + serve:static 3001). Pak: build/original/opensa rebuilt 2026-08-10 17:47 (unbaked clutter, all 95 procobj rules). ONE scene, country-dusk, five single-scene sweeps, 42 road cars. WHY: P2 — the per-category clutter draw distances. They were DEAD CONFIG (written by the debug slider, read by nothing), so every category really drew at whatever its 256-unit cell reached, and the cell ring was `streaming.collisionDrawDistance` = 150. This capture is the A/B of the range now being real: applied per INSTANCE in the clutter vertex shader, with the streaming ring widened to the widest enabled category. `?procobjRange=<units>` overrides every category with one number, which is what makes a uniform arm reproducible at all. CAVEAT ON THE CONTENT COLUMN, and it matters: `frameTriangles` counts SUBMITTED instances. The whole-group CPU skip removes a group that is entirely out of range (so draws and triangles both fall), but a group the camera stands inside is submitted whole and culled per instance in the shader — so avgTriangles UNDER-reports the fill saving and is a directional signal, not the size of the win. It is accurate about VERTEX load, blind to fill.

runs.arm: r150 — ?procobjRange=150 (the collision ring, i.e. the nearest reproducible BEFORE)
default — the shipped per-category ranges (grass/flowers/underwater 100 · bushes 150 · rocks 200 · cacti/trees 300)
r300 — ?procobjRange=300 (every category at the widest, the upper bound)

findings: THE RANGE IS REAL AND MONOTONE. Four points, one direction, no exceptions: draws 818 -> 819 -> 821 -> 830 and triangles 1 182 287 -> 1 186 367 -> 1 191 188 -> 1 209 368 for 100 / 150 / per-category / 300. The A/A control (r150 vs r150b) puts the floor at 0.020 % on triangles and ZERO on draws, so every step above is signal. Before this change the same knob moved nothing at all, because nothing read it.

IN LAYER TERMS THE RANGE IS A 4x LEVER, which the scene-scoped numbers hide. Against the clutter-off baseline of 1 173 177 triangles (from the same pak, `?procobj=0`), the layer on screen is 9 110 at range 100, 13 190 at 150, 18 011 at the shipped per-category set and 36 191 at 300. So 100 -> 300 QUADRUPLES the clutter, while reading as +2.3 % of the scene. Publish this one with its scope or it sounds like nothing.

IT IS FREE IN FRAME TERMS AT THIS SCALE. gpuMs.pass spans 3.633 - 3.694 across the whole ladder — 1.7 %, against the 6.5 % A/A drift this column showed in the same day's knob-ladder capture. avgMs is pinned at 8.33 (vsync) and every hitch column is flat: maxMs 9.5 on both the cheapest and the most expensive arm. Choosing a range is therefore a LOOK decision, not a perf one, and the r150's maxMs 26.6 / 1 slow frame is the lane's usual noise (the identical r150b read 9.5 / 0).

THE OLD BEHAVIOUR WAS NOT '150' — IT WAS 'WHATEVER CELL YOU ARE IN'. The pre-change code drew every instance of every loaded cell, and cells are 256 units, so the effective reach depended on where in the cell the camera stood — up to ~360 units at a corner. That is why the reproducible r150 arm draws LESS than the pre-change build did (819/1 186 604 vs 830/1 206 029 in the knob-ladder capture): a clean per-instance radius replaces a cell-shaped one. The gain here is determinism as much as reach.

WHAT THE NUMBERS CANNOT SAY: the look. Three headless screenshot attempts failed to find a clutter vista (a town street, a rooftop, and one spawn past the map edge that fell through the void), which is the documented hazard of judging ground-level sight lines headless. The per-category values are a judged choice awaiting the user's eyes, and the debug ProcObj sliders now actually move the world.
conclusion: The per-category ranges work, they are monotone against a 0.020 % control, and across the full 100 -> 300 span they cost nothing measurable — so the values are a look decision with a free budget, exactly as P1 predicted for this layer. The shipped set (grass/flowers/underwater 100 · bushes 150 · rocks 200 · cacti/trees 300) puts twice SA's flat-100 clutter on screen and half of what a flat 300 would, with SA's own number as the FLOOR rather than the target. Still open: the look verdict, and whether `frameTriangles` should learn to count culled instances — today it over-reports every group the camera stands inside.
